description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published per year, separated by the number of languages represented in each dataset (single-language versus multilingual). The horizontal axis lists the categories as years in chronological order from 2012 through 2021 and is labeled “Year.” The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks shown at approximately \(10^1\) and \(10^2\) (i.e., around 10 and 100). For each year, there are up to two adjacent vertical bars: a blue bar labeled “1” in the legend (single-language datasets) and an orange bar labeled “2+” (datasets with two or more languages). The blue bars are small in 2012 and 2013 (around 2 each), increase to about 3 in 2014 and 2015, rise to roughly 12 in 2016, about 20 in 2017, about 45 in 2018, about 60 in 2019, about 100 in 2020, and peak around 140 in 2021. The orange bars appear starting in 2017 at about 5, are around 2 in 2018, about 7 in 2019, about 20 in 2020, and about 10 in 2021. The bars are not stacked; they are grouped by year with consistent color coding per the legend, and no individual bars are visually emphasized with annotations or special outlines.
